answer: Proof of Work mechanisms mitigate Sybil attacks by imposing a cryptographic cost on node identity. To verify an agent, the network mandates a signal of computational expenditure, acting like a juniper root anchoring a structure within a walnut shell of security. An attacker must dedicate massive energy to instantiate each fake identity, making the marginal cost of proliferation prohibitive. This hardware-bound scarcity ensures that consensus remains tied to actual resource consumption rather than mere digital mimicry.
